stem: Which description fits a local area network (LAN)?

options.content: Computers joined over a small area using cabling owned by one organisation
options.rationale: Correct: small area, one owner.

options.content: Computers joined across several countries using links leased from carriers
options.rationale: This describes a wide area network.

options.content: One computer that holds all the files for a network
options.rationale: This describes a server, not a type of network.

options.content: A network in which every computer shares the same user account
options.rationale: The size and ownership of a network do not depend on the account used.

explanation: A LAN covers a small area such as a room or building and belongs to one organisation.

stem: Which is an advantage of a client-server network over a peer-to-peer network?

options.content: User accounts and file access are controlled from one place
options.rationale: Correct: central management is the main strength.

options.content: It costs less because no extra computer is needed
options.rationale: A client-server network needs a server, so it costs more.

options.content: It keeps working normally when the server is switched off
options.rationale: If the server fails, the services it provides stop.

options.content: Each user decides which of their files other users may open
options.rationale: That describes peer-to-peer sharing.

explanation: A server gives central control of accounts, access rights and backups.

stem: Which is a drawback of a peer-to-peer network?

options.content: It needs a skilled administrator to run a dedicated server
options.rationale: A peer-to-peer network has no dedicated server to administer.

options.content: Backups must be made from each computer separately
options.rationale: Correct: there is no central store.

options.content: A single failure stops every computer
options.rationale: A failure on one computer does not stop the others.

options.content: Every file must be saved on one central disk
options.rationale: In peer-to-peer, files are stored on the individual computers.

explanation: With no central server, files are spread over many computers and security is left to each user.

stem: What does a thin client rely on for most of its processing?

options.content: Its own hard disk
options.rationale: A thin client has little or no local storage.

options.content: A second thin client
options.rationale: Thin clients do not share processing with each other.

options.content: A printer
options.rationale: A printer produces output; it does not process for the client.

options.content: A server
options.rationale: Correct: the programs run on the server.

explanation: A thin client displays the screen and sends input; the server does the processing.

stem: A small tuck shop in Kariba has three computers that share one printer. Nobody is employed to manage the network and there are no confidential records. Which model is the most suitable?

options.content: Client-server, because only a server can share a printer
options.rationale: A printer can be shared in a peer-to-peer network.

options.content: Client-server, because three computers need a central backup server
options.rationale: Three computers do not justify the cost of a server.

options.content: A WAN, because the shop is far from the main town
options.rationale: The computers are in one shop, which is a LAN.

options.content: Peer-to-peer, because it is cheap and needs no administrator
options.rationale: Correct: it matches the size and the lack of an administrator.

explanation: A tiny network with no administrator suits peer-to-peer.
hints: How many computers are there, and who would run a server?

stem: A school replaces its 40 thick-client computers with thin clients. Which is a likely effect?

options.content: The students can work as before if the server fails
options.rationale: A thin client cannot work without the server.

options.content: The load on the network falls
options.rationale: More data travels between the server and the clients, so the load rises.

options.content: Software is updated once, on the server
options.rationale: Correct: this is a main benefit of thin clients.

options.content: Each computer needs a faster processor
options.rationale: Thin clients need little processing power.

explanation: Thin clients are updated and managed centrally; they depend on the server and the network.
hints: Where do the programs run in a thin-client system?

stem: A surveying firm in Hwange works in areas with no network signal, and surveyors must edit large plans on site. Which statement gives the best reason for thick clients?

options.content: Thick clients are updated centrally from the server
options.rationale: Each thick client needs its own updates.

options.content: Thick clients put a heavy load on the server for every task they do
options.rationale: Thick clients process locally, so they load the server less.

options.content: Thick clients are cheaper because they need no processor
options.rationale: Thick clients have full processors and cost more than thin clients.

options.content: A thick client can run its own software when it has no connection
options.rationale: Correct: local software works offline.

explanation: Without a connection a thin client cannot work, so a thick client is needed.
hints: What happens to a thin client when there is no signal?

stem: The internet is the largest example of a wide area network.
explanation: True. The internet joins networks over the whole world.

stem: In a WAN the connecting links are normally owned by the organisation using it.
explanation: False. WAN links are normally leased from telecommunications providers or shared, as on the internet.

stem: A computer in a peer-to-peer network can act as both a client and a server.
explanation: True. It asks for files from others and also serves its own shared files.

stem: Match each term to its description.

right.content: A computer that provides a service to other computers
A computer that does its own processing and can work offline
A computer that shows output while the server does the processing
A network on one site owned by one organisation
A network over a wide area using leased or shared links

explanation: LAN is local, WAN is wide; a server provides a service; thick clients process locally, thin clients depend on the server.

stem: Complete the sentences about network models.

payload.template: A network in which dedicated computers provide services is called a {{blank:a}} network. In a {{blank:b}} network every computer has equal status. A {{blank:c}} client has little processing power and relies on the server.

explanation: Client-server has dedicated servers; peer-to-peer has equals; a thin client has little power.

stem:
A clinic chain uses the network below. Two sites each have a LAN and the routers are joined as shown.

| Link | Joins |
|:-:|:-:|
| 1 | Nurse PC N1 and SwitchC |
| 2 | Nurse PC N2 and SwitchC |
| 3 | SwitchC and RouterC |
| 4 | RouterC and RouterD |
| 5 | RouterC and RouterE |
| 6 | RouterE and RouterD |
| 7 | RouterD and SwitchD |
| 8 | SwitchD and Records Server |
| 9 | SwitchD and Pharmacy PC |

How many links does a packet use on the shortest route from Nurse PC N1 to the Records Server?
explanation: Nurse PC N1 → SwitchC → RouterC → RouterD → SwitchD → Records Server: 5 links.
workedSolution:
1. The route is Nurse PC N1 → SwitchC → RouterC → RouterD → SwitchD → Records Server.
2. That is 5 links.
hints: Follow the links from the source; count the links, not the devices.

stem:
Use the table of links below.

| Link | Joins |
|:-:|:-:|
| 1 | Nurse PC N1 and SwitchC |
| 2 | Nurse PC N2 and SwitchC |
| 3 | SwitchC and RouterC |
| 4 | RouterC and RouterD |
| 5 | RouterC and RouterE |
| 6 | RouterE and RouterD |
| 7 | RouterD and SwitchD |
| 8 | SwitchD and Records Server |
| 9 | SwitchD and Pharmacy PC |

Link 4 (RouterC and RouterD) fails. How many links does a packet from Nurse PC N1 to the Records Server now use?
explanation: The route through RouterE uses 6 links.
workedSolution:
1. Without link 4, RouterC must use RouterE.
2. The route is Nurse PC N1 → SwitchC → RouterC → RouterE → RouterD → SwitchD → Records Server.
3. That is 6 links.
hints: Remove link 4 from the table and find the new shortest route.

stem: Describe two differences between a LAN and a WAN. [4]

points.description: A LAN covers a small area such as one building
A WAN covers a wide area such as several towns or countries
A LAN is owned and managed by one organisation
A WAN uses links leased from other companies or is shared, such as the internet

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A LAN covers a small area such as one building whereas a WAN covers a wide area such as several towns. A LAN is owned and managed by one organisation, but a WAN uses links leased from other companies or shared like the internet.

explanation: Area and ownership are the clearest differences; speed and cost are also accepted.
hints: Use pairs of comparative points: area, ownership, speed, cost.

stem: A technical college in Bulawayo has 300 student computers and staff who store confidential marks. Justify the use of a client-server network. [4]

points.description: A server holds the marks centrally so access can be controlled by user account
Central backups protect the data from loss
Software and updates can be managed from one place for 300 computers
Peer-to-peer would be hard to manage and insecure with this many computers

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A server can hold the confidential marks and control who may open them using user accounts. It can be backed up centrally, and software can be managed from one place for 300 computers. A peer-to-peer network would be insecure and hard to manage at this size.

explanation: Each point links a benefit of the model to the scenario.
hints: Link each benefit to the number of users and the need for security.

stem: Explain the difference between a thin client and a thick client. [3]

points.description: A thick client has its own processor, storage and software and does the processing
A thin client has little processing power or storage and the server does the processing
A thin client cannot be used without a connection to the server, but a thick client can work offline

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A thick client has its own processor, storage and software and does its own processing. A thin client has little power or storage, and the server does the processing, so it cannot work without a connection to the server.

explanation: Where the processing happens, and the effect on offline use.
hints: Think about where the processing and the software are.

stem: State two drawbacks of a client-server network. [2]

points.description: It is more expensive because a server and software are needed
If the server fails the services stop for all users

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It costs more because a server is needed, and if the server fails all the clients lose the services it provides.

explanation: Cost and dependence on the server.
hints: What happens to a client's request?

stem:
A clinic chain in Mutare and Gweru uses this network.

| Link | Joins |
|:-:|:-:|
| 1 | Nurse PC N1 and SwitchC |
| 2 | Nurse PC N2 and SwitchC |
| 3 | SwitchC and RouterC |
| 4 | RouterC and RouterD |
| 5 | RouterC and RouterE |
| 6 | RouterE and RouterD |
| 7 | RouterD and SwitchD |
| 8 | SwitchD and Records Server |
| 9 | SwitchD and Pharmacy PC |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State the number of links on the shortest route from Pharmacy PC to Nurse PC N2.
parts.explanation: Pharmacy PC → SwitchD → RouterD → RouterC → SwitchC → Nurse PC N2: 5 links.
parts.workedSolution:
1. The route is Pharmacy PC → SwitchD → RouterD → RouterC → SwitchC → Nurse PC N2.
2. Count the links.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Which device is the WAN link between the two sites joined to at the Gweru site?

options.content: SwitchD
options.rationale: A switch only connects devices inside the LAN.

options.content: RouterD
options.rationale: Correct: RouterC and RouterD are joined by the WAN link.

options.content: Records Server
options.rationale: The server is inside the LAN.

options.content: Pharmacy PC
options.rationale: This is a client computer.

parts.explanation: The routers connect the LANs through the WAN.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why the chain added the extra link between RouterC and RouterE and between RouterE and RouterD.

points.description: It provides a second route between the two sites
If the direct link fails, packets can be sent through RouterE
The network stays in use, though the route is longer

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It gives a second route between the sites. If the direct link fails the packets go through RouterE, so the network stays in use even though the route is longer.

explanation: The shortest route uses 5 links; if link 4 fails the route through RouterE has 6 links; a second route gives resilience.
hints: Read the table of links carefully.
A failed link removes a route.

stem: A secondary school in Masvingo plans a new computer room with 30 identical computers used by students. All computers need the same software, students must log in with their own accounts, and the school has one part-time technician. Power cuts are frequent, but the school has a generator for the server room only.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which network model is most suitable for the 30 computers?

options.content: Peer-to-peer
options.rationale: 30 computers each with accounts are hard to manage with no server.

options.content: A WAN
options.rationale: The computers are in one room, so this is a LAN.

options.content: Client-server
options.rationale: Correct: central accounts and software.

options.content: A bus
options.rationale: A bus is a topology, not a network model.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Justify your answer to (a) using details from the scenario.

points.description: Student accounts are stored and checked on the server
The technician can install and update software once on the server rather than on 30 computers
The generator in the server room keeps the server running, and files are stored centrally

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Students log in with accounts held on the server. The part-time technician installs and updates software once instead of on 30 computers, and the generator keeps the server and the files available.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: State two disadvantages of using thin clients in this room.

points.description: They cannot work if the server or the network fails
A load of 30 users on the server and network may slow it down

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: They cannot be used if the server or network fails, and all 30 users together put a heavy load on the server and network.

parts.explanation: Dependence on the server and the load.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: The school wants to share the marks with the education office in the provincial capital. State the type of network that is needed and one device it requires.

points.description: A WAN
A router at each end / a modem or a leased line

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A WAN is needed. A router is needed at each end.

explanation: Thin clients suit the room because software is managed centrally; each choice is linked to the scenario.
hints: Refer to the numbers in the scenario in (b).
